node.title: Fixed-kernel rate-half Hankel branch
node.statement: Let rho>=1 be the generic rank of an RS syndrome Hankel pencil. If its generic right kernel is the scalar extension of a fixed F-subspace K_0, then K_0 is annihilated by both endpoint matrices. For a column-far pair K_0 contains no domain-split locator. Away from the roots of one nonzero rho-minor, specialization preserves rank and the kernel remains K_0. Hence at most rho finite slopes carry a split locator. This closes every constant-kernel rank-deficient branch, including at the half-distance endpoint; only genuinely moving generic kernels remain.
